correctness.rationale: Poisson thinning makes independent site-success indicators with failure u_i=exp(−a x_i) for the two strong sites and v=exp(−b x_3). For fixed weak effort x3, total success P=1−(1−r)(u1+u2)+(1−2r)u1u2; u1u2 fixed, strict AM–GM gives unique x1=x2. Set B=aE,h=b/a,z=ax3,u=exp(−(B−z)/2),v=exp(−hz). Failure F=u²+2u(1−u)v has exact derivative u[u(1−v)+(1−2h)v(1−u)]. For h≤1/2 derivative positive interior and zero optimal weak effort; h>1/2 derivative changes uniquely negative to positive because (exp(hz)−1)/(exp((B−z)/2)−1) rises from zero to infinity. Small-budget root ratio gives (2h−1)/(4h−1); large-budget logarithms give z=[B+2log(2h−1)]/(2h+1)+o(1). Independent sympy differentiation returned zero difference and scalar numerical optima at h=.25,.5,.75,1, B=.2,3,30 agreed with regime. Numeric tests not substituted for global continuous proof.
